_meta.title: CCNA 模拟考试（60题 · 六大域配比）

questions.text: Which OSI layer do switches operate at?
questions.explanation: Switches operate at Layer 2 using MAC addresses. Hubs are Layer 1. Routers are Layer 3.

questions.text: How many usable hosts in a /26 subnet?
questions.explanation: /26 = 6 host bits. 2^6=64 total, minus 2 = 62 usable.

questions.text: Which TCP flag starts the three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: The client sends SYN to initiate. Server responds SYN-ACK. Client sends ACK.

questions.text: What is the binary of 192?
When a switch receives a frame with an unknown destination MAC, what does it do?
options: C. Floods all ports except received
questions.explanation: Unknown unicast flooding sends the frame to all ports except the receiving port. The switch learns from any reply.

questions.text: Describe the CSMA/CD process used by half-duplex Ethernet.
options: A. Carrier sense with collision detection
questions.explanation: CSMA/CD listens before transmitting and detects collisions. Token passing is Token Ring. Modern Ethernet uses full-duplex.

questions.text: Which address range is used for APIPA?
questions.explanation: APIFA (169.254.0.0/16) is auto-assigned by Windows when DHCP fails. The other ranges are RFC 1918 private addresses.

questions.text: Two buildings 60km apart need 10Gbps connectivity. Which fiber?
questions.explanation: Single-mode OS2 supports 10G over 40-80km. OM4 MMF reaches 550m at 10G. Cat6a is limited to 100m.

questions.text: A network needs 500 subnets from 10.0.0.0/8 with 100+ hosts each. Which mask?
What does a wildcard mask of 0.0.0.255 match?
questions.explanation: 0=must match, 1=ignore. 0.0.0.255 matches the first 24 bits exactly, ignoring the last 8.

questions.text: Which statement about CRC errors is correct?
questions.explanation: CRC errors indicate corrupted frames, almost always physical layer issues (cable, EMI). Duplex mismatch causes runts/collisions.

questions.text: What is a characteristic of UDP?
questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless with minimal overhead. TCP provides guaranteed delivery, sequencing, and windowing.

questions.text: What is the effect of "switchport port-security maximum 2 violation restrict"?
options: B. Only 2 MACs; violations logged but port stays up
questions.explanation: Restrict mode drops violations, logs them, and keeps the port up. Shutdown mode error-disables the port. Police mode drops silently.

questions.text: On an 802.1Q trunk, native VLAN frames are:
questions.explanation: Native VLAN frames are sent untagged on 802.1Q trunks. This allows legacy devices to connect to trunk ports.

questions.text: Which feature lets access ports skip STP listening/learning?
questions.explanation: PortFast immediately transitions to forwarding on access ports. BPDU Guard error-disables on BPDU reception. Root Guard prevents root bridge election.

questions.text: In RSTP, which port immediately takes over when the root port fails?
questions.explanation: The Alternate Port provides a backup path to the root bridge. In RSTP it transitions to forwarding immediately without listening/learning.

questions.text: Which LACP mode initiates negotiations?
questions.explanation: LACP Active sends negotiation packets. Passive only responds. "On" is static without negotiation. "Auto" is PAgP (Cisco proprietary).

questions.text: Inter-VLAN routing requires:
questions.explanation: VLANs are separate broadcast domains. A Layer 3 device (router or Layer 3 switch with SVI) is required for inter-VLAN routing.

questions.text: Which IEEE standard defines RSTP?
questions.explanation: 802.1w = RSTP (fast convergence). 802.1D = original STP. 802.1s = MSTP. 802.1Q = VLAN trunking.

questions.text: What does "show interfaces trunk" display?
options: A. Allowed VLANs on trunk links
questions.explanation: It displays trunking status, native VLAN, and allowed VLANs per trunk link. Essential for verifying trunk configuration.

questions.text: PortFast + BPDU Guard: receiving a BPDU causes:
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard error-disables a port that receives any BPDU. This prevents unauthorized switch connections on access ports.

questions.text: What is the Split-MAC architecture in Cisco wireless?
options: A. AP handles data, WLC handles management
questions.explanation: Split-MAC separates real-time data (AP) from management/control (WLC). This is the foundation of Cisco unified wireless.

questions.text: Which command enables 802.1Q trunking on a Catalyst switch?
options: B. switchport mode trunk; encapsulation dot1q
questions.explanation: "switchport mode trunk" + "switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q" enables 802.1Q trunking. Access mode prevents trunking.

questions.text: Which protocol dynamically assigns VLANs based on MAC address?
questions.explanation: VMPS (VLAN Membership Policy Server) assigns ports to VLANs based on source MAC. VTP distributes VLAN configs. DTP negotiates trunks.

questions.text: EIGRP has AD 90, OSPF has AD 110. Which route is preferred?
questions.explanation: Lower administrative distance is preferred. EIGRP (90) beats OSPF (110). AD is compared between different protocols, metric within same protocol.
The 200 is the administrative distance, making this a floating static route used only if the primary route (with lower AD) fails.

questions.text: On Ethernet, how does OSPF reduce adjacencies?
questions.explanation: DR/BDR election reduces full adjacencies from n(n-1)/2 to 2n-3 on broadcast multi-access networks.

questions.text: Which FHRP is an open standard?
questions.explanation: VRRP is an open standard (RFC 5798). HSRP and GLBP are Cisco proprietary. IRDP is an obsolete discovery protocol.

questions.text: Default OSPF Hello timer on broadcast networks:
questions.explanation: OSPF Hello defaults to 10s on broadcast and point-to-point networks. 30s on NBMA. Dead timer is 4x Hello (40s).

questions.text: What is the default OSPF cost of a Gigabit Ethernet?
questions.explanation: Default reference bandwidth is 100Mbps. Cost = 100/1000 = 0.1, rounded to 1. This is why adjusting the reference bandwidth is often needed.

questions.text: Router R1 has a floating static route with AD 200. EIGRP learns the same route. Which is used?
questions.explanation: The EIGRP route (AD 90) is used while available. If it fails, the floating static (AD 200) becomes active as a backup.

questions.text: Which route has AD 0?
questions.explanation: Connected interfaces have AD 0 (highest priority). Static routes have AD 1. OSPF 110. EIGRP internal 90.

questions.text: OSPF neighbor shows "Init" state. What does this mean?
options: B. Hello received, but own RID not seen
questions.explanation: Init means Hello received from neighbor, but neighbor has not yet seen this router's RID in its Hellos. Next state is 2WAY.

questions.text: In OSPF, what does an ABR generate?
questions.explanation: ABRs generate Type 3 (Summary) LSAs to advertise networks between areas. Type 1 = Router LSA. Type 5 = AS External.

questions.text: Which FHRP allows multiple routers to forward simultaneously?
questions.explanation: GLBP provides active-active forwarding with load balancing. HSRP/VRRP have one active router at a time with standby/backup.

questions.text: What does "ip classless" enable?
options: A. Routing to unknown subnets of known networks
questions.explanation: ip classless allows forwarding packets using the default route when the destination is a subnet of a known network not in the routing table.

questions.text: How is an IPv6 default route configured?
questions.explanation: IPv6 default route uses ::/0. The syntax is "ipv6 route ::/0 interface next-hop".

questions.text: Type 3 LSAs carry:
questions.explanation: Type 3 LSAs carry inter-area routes, generated by ABRs. Type 5 carries external routes. Type 1 describes router interfaces.

questions.text: ECMP in OSPF: maximum paths default?
questions.explanation: Default maximum-paths in OSPF is typically 4 on Cisco IOS. The "maximum-paths" command controls equal-cost multipathing.

questions.text: DHCPDISCOVER is sent as:
questions.explanation: DHCPDISCOVER is a broadcast (255.255.255.255) sent by clients to find DHCP servers. DORA: Discover, Offer, Request, Ack.

questions.text: What does NTP synchronize?
questions.explanation: NTP synchronizes clocks on network devices. Essential for log correlation, authentication, and troubleshooting.

questions.text: Which SNMP version uses community strings in plaintext?
questions.explanation: SNMPv1 and v2c use plaintext community strings. SNMPv3 provides authentication and encryption for security.

questions.text: What is the purpose of QoS EF (Expedited Forwarding)?
questions.explanation: EF (DSCP 46) provides low-loss, low-latency, low-jitter service, typically used for voice traffic.

questions.text: A DHCP server responds to a DISCOVER with what message?
questions.explanation: The server responds with DHCPOFFER containing an available IP address. The client then sends DHCPREQUEST to accept.

questions.text: NTP client syncing to stratum 3 becomes:
questions.explanation: Stratum increments by 1 per hop. Client syncing to stratum 3 becomes stratum 4. Stratum 1 is an authoritative time source.

questions.text: Extended ACLs should be placed:
questions.explanation: Extended ACLs are placed closest to the source to filter traffic early. Standard ACLs are placed near the destination.

questions.text: An attacker connects a switch to an access port and becomes STP root. Which feature prevents this?
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard error-disables a port receiving BPDUs on an access port. Root Guard prevents a port from becoming root but does not error-disable.

questions.text: Which attack exhausts the DHCP pool with fake requests?
questions.explanation: DHCP starvation floods the server with fake requests to exhaust the address pool. DHCP Snooping mitigates this.

questions.text: What is the final entry in every ACL?
questions.explanation: Every ACL has an implicit "deny any any" at the end. At least one permit entry must exist to allow traffic.

questions.text: AAA stands for:
questions.explanation: AAA: Authentication (who you are), Authorization (what you can do), Accounting (what you did).

questions.text: What is the function of DHCP Snooping?
options: A. Filters DHCP messages from untrusted ports
questions.explanation: DHCP Snooping filters DHCP server messages from untrusted (access) ports and builds a binding database of valid IP-MAC mappings.

questions.text: Which type of firewall tracks connection state?
questions.explanation: A stateful firewall maintains a state table of active connections, allowing return traffic for established sessions.

questions.text: Cisco TrustSec uses which tags for identity-based policies?
questions.explanation: Security Group Tags identify users/devices for role-based access control, independent of IP addresses.

questions.text: Control Plane Policing (CoPP) protects what?
questions.explanation: CoPP protects the route processor by rate-limiting traffic directed to the control plane, preventing CPU overload.

questions.text: What is the primary use of JSON in network automation?
options: A. Data interchange in REST APIs
questions.explanation: JSON is the standard data format for REST API requests and responses in network automation. Lightweight and human-readable.

questions.text: In Cisco DNA Center, which component translates business intent into network config?
questions.explanation: The Policy component translates intent (e.g., voice priority) into device configuration. Design creates profiles. Provision deploys. Assurance monitors.

questions.text: Which data format uses indentation for hierarchy (Ansible playbooks)?
questions.explanation: YAML uses indentation with spaces for hierarchy. It is the default format for Ansible playbooks and Kubernetes manifests.

questions.text: What transport does NETCONF use?
questions.explanation: NETCONF uses SSH (port 830) as its secure transport. RESTCONF uses HTTP/HTTPS. Both access YANG data models.

questions.text: Which Python library simplifies SSH connections to network devices?
questions.explanation: Netmiko simplifies SSH connections with a consistent API across vendors. Requests handles HTTP. Flask is a web framework.

questions.text: What is the purpose of git in network automation?
questions.explanation: Git provides version control for config files and automation scripts, enabling change tracking, collaboration, and rollback.
